author: Mark Atwood
text:
Architectural decision deferred to human. Reshape Invocation from 3-tuple (String, Value, String) to a named-field struct.

Cost / propagation:
- Foundation-type reshape in jmap-types. Per workspace AGENTS.md jmap-types canonical-template rule, this 'ripples through every downstream jmap-* crate' and 'every break here is amplified seven times by the extension-types crates and seven more times by the extension-server / extension-client crates'.
- The current 3-tuple serializes/deserializes for free via serde-tuple-as-JSON-array, which matches the RFC 8620 §3.3 wire format [method, args, callId] verbatim. Reshaping to a struct requires manual Serialize/Deserialize impls to preserve wire shape.
- Workspace-wide use sites: .0 / .1 / .2 indexing across crate-jmap-server (dispatcher loop) + every test that constructs an Invocation by tuple literal + every method-call destructuring.

Benefits:
- Reader sees .method / .args / .call_id instead of .0 / .1 / .2. Real readability win.

Bead author confidence (in epic body): low — 'may be intentional to match JMAP wire serialization shape verbatim and minimize Value materialization'.

Decision needed: (a) keep current shape (3-tuple matches wire form; documented), (b) schedule the reshape for the next workspace major bump along with other breaking-API reshapes (JMAP-wlip.24, JMAP-wlip.34, JMAP-wlip.35, JMAP-wlip.36), or (c) reshape now and pay the workspace-wide propagation cost.

Recommendation: (b) — pair the reshape with the next planned major. Either keep the named-field struct AND add a custom Serialize/Deserialize for wire-array form, or introduce a NamedInvocation alongside the tuple for ergonomic construction without breaking serialization.
